Balanced tone, lots of sustain, harmonics and a ton of fuzz makes the Ram's Head a favorite among fuzz users. This version has warm, creamy, fuzz that make chords evenly balanced and full while retaining string clarity. Lead tones are very smooth, punchy and warm as harmonics jump out with very little effort. sources.excerpt: 2247 Ram's HEad v8 by Stomp Under Foot | RockBoard | PedalPedia Skip to main content LOG IN EXPLORE Stomp Under Foot 2247 Ram's HEad v8 LOG IN TO SUGGEST IMPROVEMENTS FUZZ Description The Stomp Under Foot - 1973 "2247" Ram's Head is based on a rare version of a 1973 Ram's Head that makes it unique among the pedals of the time. Large-value and larger in physical size capacitors give it a big and open tone, crunchy and clear. Turning down the gain delivers a fuzzy/overdriven tone that sound great. As always Stomp Under Foot features through-hole components, and this '2247' sports NOS resistors and capacitors as found in the original 1973 version.
